**2026-10-21 evidence and appearance cohort — the terminal's own colours, the
audit's own durability, and the costs that are stated rather than hidden:**

- [x] The TUI asks the terminal for its background and reads the answer
      without eating the user's keystrokes: the read is a byte at a time and
      stops at the reply's terminator, the descriptor is non-blocking only
      for the duration of the read and its flags are restored afterwards, and
      a terminal that answers after the window is given a short grace. A
      reply that started and was cut short is exactly the case the grace
      exists for. Evidence: the 25 unit tests in
      `src/tui/terminal_appearance.rs`, including
      `the_read_stops_at_the_terminator_and_leaves_the_keystrokes_after_it`,
      `the_terminals_own_flags_are_restored_after_the_query`,
      `a_reply_that_arrives_after_the_window_is_taken_by_the_grace`, and
      `a_terminal_that_never_answers_is_waited_on_only_for_the_bound`.
- [x] The query's residual costs are stated, not hidden: the module no longer
      claims that a late answer can never reach the composer. It cannot — once
      the bytes are in the event queue the app cannot tell an `OSC` reply from
      typed text — and a terminal that answers later than the grace has its
      reply read as key events. A keystroke that lands inside the query
      window is still lost, because the terminal's input queue cannot be put
      back. The receipt states both, and the Windows path keeps the dark
      palette because the question is not asked there at all.
- [x] The palette is measured, not asserted: brightness is classified by WCAG
      relative luminance rather than by a channel average, and every palette
      is checked against the contrast ratio (at least 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1
      for UI borders). A colour that stops being legible fails the build.
      Evidence: `src/tui/theme.rs::relative_luminance`,
      `src/tui/theme.rs::every_palette_is_legible`, and the saturated-green
      classification test.
- [x] A lost routing-audit record is a hole in the evidence, not a detail:
      the record is now written with an error that fails the turn, and the
      write is synced — a successful `write` only reaches the page cache, and
      a sync failure loses the record with no error at all. The activity row
      beside it stays best-effort on purpose, because it is a learning input
      and losing one must not fail a turn that can answer. The subagent lanes
      carry the same rule. Evidence:
      `tests/cli_surface.rs::an_unwritable_route_log_fails_the_turn_instead_of_losing_the_record`
      and `tests/cli_surface.rs::print_bypasses_the_route_log_where_ask_appends`.
- [x] The instruction-shape checker no longer reads a shell comment as a
      heading: fenced code blocks are skipped, so a `#` comment line inside
      the command table is a comment. Evidence:
      `tools/tests/test_check_instructions.py::test_a_comment_inside_the_command_block_is_not_a_heading`
      and `::test_a_heading_after_a_fenced_block_is_still_reported`.
- [x] The fixtures tell "not observed" apart from "observed to be wrong": the
      provider PTY smoke test retries only an indeterminate observation and
      gives each attempt its own directory, and the CLI surface fixture is
      hermetic — it removes the ambient live-context recipe variable and
      reports the child's stderr and the state directory's listing when an
      assertion fails. Evidence:
      `tools/tests/smoke_tui_provider_pty.py::observed` and the
      `tests/cli_surface.rs` route-log assertions.
- [x] Two claim rows were corrected to say what the code does: `backend-ollama`
      now states that Abbey never auto-pulls (every spawn path preflights
      `ollama list` and a missing tag fails the turn), and
      `daemon-protocol-v3-exact-model-inference` now states that the duration
      ceiling is consulted at the run's event checkpoints, so a cold device
      that compiles before its first event can outlast it and the client's
      read deadline is the effective bound.
- [x] The desktop window is one piece of native glass: the safety panel is
      opaque (`setTransparent(false)`), the material is inserted above it
      (`NSWindowOrderingMode::Above`), and the material's autoresizing mask

- [ ] **Not proven by the gate:** the Accessibility control driver

## Approved capability expansion roadmap (Proposed, not Current)

Implementation order is dependency-driven. Every user-facing refusal remains exit 2
until its slice has tests and runtime evidence; checking a design subtask does not promote
the parent capability to Current.

- [ ] **1. Runtime contracts:** define provider-neutral executor, tool-call, permission,
      cancellation, transcript, and audit interfaces; adapt current cursor/abi/fm/grok
      backends behind them without reimplementing vendor runtimes.
  - [x] Foundation: extract a reusable library, stable `AppCommand`/`AppEvent`/ID/status/
        capability contracts, standard read-only policy, and authenticated bounded Unix
        `abbeyd` Status/Claims transport plus `abbey daemon status|claims` client with
        real-binary human/JSON, no-executor, correlation, invariant, and redaction proof.
        This does not complete executor/tool/cancellation, durable-job, Windows named-pipe,
        or memory-ownership work.
  - [x] ABI adoption foundation: CI pins the merged ABI foundation train at
        `88c02fb550169e4cdb5e1df2bf6d1d13532e0e49`; Abbey compiles the additive
        agent-host, agent-runtime, model-registry, local-model-runtime, and worker
        crates as sibling dependencies. Durable execution now shares ABI's cooperative
        cancellation token, and `ModelProviderExecutor` binds closed Abbey backends to
        startup-owned ABI `ModelProvider` objects, exact model IDs, and finite event,
        token, duration, and capture bounds. It rejects unbound routes, model
        substitution, tool events, malformed event order, duplicate backends, and
        provider-detail disclosure. This bridge is not wired into daemon authority yet,
        adds no protocol command, and does not promote the Proposed runtime claim.
  - [x] Desktop ABI lock synchronization: refresh `desktop/Cargo.lock` after the five
        ABI runtime dependencies entered Abbey's shared library graph. The deterministic
        lock now resolves the same sibling crates as the root build, and the complete
        desktop codegen, TypeScript, bundle-security, default/personal, configured-daemon
        refusal, and real-link gate passes with `--locked`. This is dependency hygiene,
        not a new desktop view or runtime capability.
  - [x] Fixed-recipe provider adapters: Cursor, Grok, ABI-local, and Foundation
        Models now implement ABI's `ModelProvider` through the existing Abbey argv
        builders and bounded process-group supervisor. Startup owns the canonical
        executable, exact model, workspace, benign environment, and all limits.
        Requests cannot supply tools, system overrides, token hints, flag-shaped
        options, alternate models, executables, argv, environment, or workspaces.
        The ABI-local adapter accepts only `local`; Foundation Models accepts only
        exact `system` or `pcc`. The adapters are not daemon-wired or advertised by
        protocol v1/v2, and vendor token usage remains unclaimed because those CLIs
        do not expose a trustworthy tokenizer count at this boundary.
  - [x] Protocol-v3 contract foundation: define a separate v3 command/event family for
        explicit grant negotiation, tools and digest-bound decisions, memory, immutable
        model revisions, reproducible training, workers/jobs, stable claim IDs, bounded
        errors, and fixed-watermark polling. Canonical grants deny by default, reject
        duplicate/reordered wire input, and cannot exceed the request. Protocol v1/v2
        enums and fixtures remain byte-compatible; `APP_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 2 and
        `abbeyd` still supports only `[1, 2]`, so this adds no dispatch or advertised v3
        authority. The next slice must add an authenticated v3 envelope and negotiate
        only the first daemon-owned route it actually implements.
- [ ] **2. Owned tool host:** implement capability-scoped tool registry plus MCP/ACP host
      adapters, schema validation, bounded subprocess/network policy, consent, and audit;
      preserve current inventory/peer-launch behavior during migration.
- [ ] **3. Desktop GUI:** add a Tauri 2 + React/TypeScript frontend over shared
      session/application state, not a second engine; cover backend selection, chat, tools/consent, memory,
      routes, and accessibility while keeping CLI/TUI supported.
- [ ] **4. Local model runtime:** integrate production-capable local weights through an
      ABI-owned inference contract with model manifests, integrity/license provenance,
      deterministic CPU fallback, memory budgets, and measurable quality/performance bars.
- [ ] **5. Accelerator runtime:** add GPU/NPU/TPU capability negotiation and execution
      behind the same compute abstraction; test numerical correctness and fallbacks before
      advertising compilation/training/inference support.
      — _partially real as of 2026-08-09 — the item stays open._ **Now Current (narrow):**
      `abbey accel verify` behind off-by-default `--features accel` runs three numerical
      kernels (`dot`, `cosine`, `top_k`; 1024-element f32) through ABI's `MetalAccelerator`
      and checks each natively produced value against the `abi-compute` `CpuBackend` oracle
      in the same run — floats at relative tolerance `1e-3` vs `max(|native|,|oracle|,1.0)`,
      `top_k` indices exactly. Execution is read from the adapter's `CapabilityState` ladder
      (fresh adapter per kernel), never from the return value, because the adapter returns
      the oracle itself on fallback. Live-verified on Apple Silicon: `backend used gpu-metal`,
      all three `match`, exit 0. Claim: `accelerator-kernel-execution-metal`.
      **Still Proposed and untouched** (`accelerator-execution-runtime`): capability
      _negotiation_ (there is no selection policy — the kernel set is fixed and Metal-only);
      GPU/NPU/TPU **compilation, training, and model inference**; ANE/NPU residency or
      placement (a Metal or CoreML output-oracle success proves execution under a requested
      compute-unit policy, **not** placement — see the recorded lesson); CUDA/Vulkan/TPU,
      whose ABI adapters stay build-detection only; and any speedup or performance figure —
      nothing on this path is timed, and none was measured.
      — _installation gap closed 2026-08-10:_ `install.sh` now treats the CLI, Unix daemon,
      and `libabi_metal_dot.dylib` as one rollback-protected publication unit. It verifies
      both executable dependencies and the dylib identity as
      `@loader_path/libabi_metal_dot.dylib` with `otool`, executes the exact staged and
      installed layouts, and refuses unsupported/unverifiable platforms before publishing.
      The isolated-install fixture proves native Metal/oracle success from the installed
      binary and proves staged-verification plus mid-relocation failures leave all three
      prior destination files byte-identical with no staging residue.
- [ ] **6. LoRA/fine-tuning:** promote curated `train_candidate` data through explicit
      consent/redaction/splits, reproducible adapter training, evaluation, rollback, and
      signed artifact provenance; no automatic weight mutation.
- [ ] **7. Local neural media:** implement speech first, then image/video through the
      model/runtime/accelerator contracts; preserve platform voice and delegated-agent
      generation as clearly distinct Current paths.
- [ ] **8. Shared compute + separate edition:** first prove authenticated shared compute
      across three local VMs on one Mac (identity, quorum, leases, failure recovery,
      observability) from ABI primitives. Keep separate-physical-host, geographic-HA, and
      multi-GPU production operation Proposed after that proof. Package the
      personal-unrestricted edition separately with local control,
      isolation, auditable consent, and no bypass path in standard Abbey.

        The 2026-08-09 failure asserted a bare `is_file()` at a line the file has since

    - **The observer used a different rule than the recovery path.**
      `wait_for_pending` read `Path::is_file()`, which _follows symlinks_: a dangling
      `pending.json` reads as "no marker" even though the marker exists. The recovery
      path itself (`src/state/conversation.rs::remove_pending`) reads
      `fs::symlink_metadata` and requires a _regular file_. The observer now uses the
      recovery path's exact rule, and a new regression test
      (`the_pending_marker_observer_uses_the_recovery_paths_rule`) pins it with a
      dangling symlink and a real regular file.
    - **The barrier bound was too tight.** `BARRIER_TIMEOUT` was two seconds, and the
      fixture waits on real processes writing real files; under load a bounded wait
      becomes a false failure. It is now fifteen seconds — still a bounded wait, and
      a genuinely broken recovery still fails promptly.
      Verified by re-running the suite serially (`--test-threads=1`) and in parallel,
      with all four cases passing in both. This closes the _observer_ defects; the

  - **Supervisor teardown flakes diagnosed and fixed 2026-08-09 (`71f2903`):**
    Measured on `bfe364e` with 12 full `cargo test` iterations — **3/12 runs failed
    (25%)**:
    - `runtime::supervisor::tests::timeout_and_precancelled_execution_teardown_the_group`
      2/12 — `Teardown("process group survived SIGKILL grace")`
    - `runtime::supervisor::tests::exact_cap_succeeds_and_cap_plus_one_fails_closed_for_both_streams`
      1/12 — `Teardown("send SIGTERM to process group was not permitted")`

    One root cause, and it is a **fixture** defect, not a containment defect.
    `group_exists` is `killpg(pgid, 0)`; on Darwin an unreaped zombie still answers it
    (with success, or with the EPERM `signal_group_until` retries). A group member
    orphaned by its dying leader is reparented to launchd and reaped _asynchronously_,
    so the group stays observable after every process in it is dead. `terminate` waits
    for the group to vanish and fails closed at `terminate_grace`, so at 100ms (30ms in
    the timeout test) the fixture was asserting that launchd reaps within 100ms —
    something neither test is about and neither can schedule.
    First fix: `terminate_grace` bounds a poll-until-gone loop, not a sleep — `terminate`
    rechecks every `poll_interval` and returns the moment the group is gone, so raising
    the bound costs an idle machine nothing. `TEARDOWN_GRACE` = 1s (cap is 5s), the
    30ms override dropped, and the `elapsed() < 2s` liveness bounds raised to
    `LIVENESS_BOUND` = 10s so the same race cannot relocate into them.
    **After: 0/15** full-suite iterations failed. **Train 1.4 follow-up
    (2026-08-10):** a real child-group fixture now reaches the precise direct-leader
    zombie state deterministically: the pipe reaches EOF, while `killpg(pgid, 0)`
    still reports the unreaped leader's group. `ChildGuard::terminate` now reaps that
    leader before its final post-SIGKILL liveness decision; the fixture passes and the
    false `process group survived SIGKILL grace` classification is closed for this
    owned-child boundary. **Second Train 1.4 follow-up (2026-08-10):** the complete gate
    later produced one `capture pipes remained open after process-group teardown` failure
    while 50 isolated repetitions passed. Reader collection therefore got its own doubled
    scheduling window, capped by the existing five-second teardown maximum. **2026-08-19
    correction:** the original 30 ms delayed-reader fixture was not deterministic: its
    worker sleeps began only when the OS scheduled each worker, while the collector's 40 ms
    deadline began immediately. The personal-edition full suite and a 200-run, 32-way stress
    reproduction exposed that race. The test now pins the extracted production window
    calculation directly instead of asserting scheduler timing. Process-group deadlines
    remain unchanged and a genuine pipe leak still fails within a fixed bound.

  - **`daemon::client::tests::real_scratch_server_round_trip` EINVAL — resolved by
    deterministic handoff coverage (2026-08-10):** reported once as
    `Configure(Os { code: 22, InvalidInput })`. Two hypotheses are now _disproven_:
    it is not Rust's zero-`Duration` rejection (that is a constructed `io::Error`, not
    an `Os` errno), and it is not `sun_path` truncation (the client's socket path is
    `/tmp/adc-<label>-<pid>-<8hex>/abbeyd.sock` = **40 bytes**, against Darwin's 104
    cap — `client.rs::scratch_dir` already uses `/tmp` for this reason).
    What _is_ proven, by direct probe: on Darwin `setsockopt(SO_RCVTIMEO)` against a
    UDS whose peer has closed returns **EINVAL (22)**. The matching code path is real —
    `DaemonClient` performs `UnixStream::connect` on a worker thread and only sets the
    timeouts on the main thread _after_ an mpsc handoff, while the daemon applies its
    own 300ms `read_timeout` to `read_frame`; a >300ms scheduling stall across that
    handoff lets the daemon close first, so the client's `set_read_timeout` lands on a
    closed peer.
    Train 1.4 injects a barrier immediately after `connect`, closes the accepted peer,
    and releases the client only after the peer is gone. This deterministically reaches
    the same handoff race: Darwin can fail timeout configuration with `EINVAL`, while
    other Unix hosts can reach the first write and fail there. Connection establishment
    now includes timeout configuration plus the first complete framed write and flush
    inside the bounded worker; every peer-close outcome in that handoff maps to one
    stable `ConnectionHandoff` error. The race fixture and the real scratch round trip
    both pass, so the old platform-error leak is closed without pretending the peer
    stayed alive.

  - **Slice 1 shipped (`mcp-server-stdio-readonly`, `src/mcp_host/`, `abbey mcp serve`):**

    whose effect type admits read-only tools only. Enforced named limits:
    `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES`, `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`, `MAX_JSON_DEPTH`, `MAX_BATCH_SIZE`,
    `MAX_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, `MAX_TOOL_NAME_BYTES`. Outbound secret redaction runs over
    the serialized frame. Note this makes Abbey an MCP **server**; being a client/host
    of _other_ providers' MCP servers stays `runtime-provider-neutral-owned` (Proposed).
  - **Slice 2 shipped (`mcp-server-http-loopback-readonly`, `src/mcp_host/http/`,
    `abbey mcp serve http`) — REAL:** HTTP/1.1 `POST /mcp`, one request per connection
    (`Connection: close`), routed through the _same_ `Server::handle_frame` and
    `Server::encode_frame` as stdio, so the registry, ceilings, and redaction are shared
    rather than forked. Bind is loopback-only and a non-loopback `--host` is a hard
    startup error. Two-layer DNS-rebinding defense: `Host` must be loopback (works with
    no `Origin` at all) and `Origin`, when present, must be a loopback origin — both
    parsed with the `url` crate, never substring-matched. New enforced named limits, each
    with a threshold test: `MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`, `MAX_REQUESTS_PER_WINDOW`,
    `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW`, `HTTP_READ_TIMEOUT`, `HTTP_WRITE_TIMEOUT`, `MAX_HTTP_HEAD_BYTES`,
    `MAX_HTTP_HEADERS`, `MAX_HTTP_SESSIONS`, `HTTP_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT`. Threaded
    `std::net::TcpListener` — no async stack and no new dependency was added.
  - **REAL but bounded — say it plainly:** the HTTP transport is _unauthenticated_.
    Loopback-only bounds _who can reach it_ (no off-host caller), not _who may call it_
    (any local process may, while it runs). `Mcp-Session-Id` is a routing key, not a
    credential. OAuth 2.1/PKCE is not required for a loopback socket and was deliberately
    **not faked** — there is no token, no PKCE exchange, and no `WWW-Authenticate`
    anywhere in the module, asserted by
    `tests/mcp_http.rs::the_transport_refuses_what_it_does_not_implement`.

- [x] `abbey memory reflect` / learn digest (duplicates / low-confidence listing)

### Phase 3 — WDBX bridge

- [x] Feature `wdbx`: optional path-dep `abi-wdbx`; `WdbxMemory` implements the full
      `MemoryStore` trait over `DurableStore` KV (records as JSON under `mem/<id>`)
- [x] Backend dispatch: `memory::open_backend` → `Box<dyn MemoryStore>`; all call sites
      (session/learn/doctor/tui) route through config `memory_backend`
- [x] Fallback: `abbey wdbx <query|db|…>` subprocess to `abi wdbx …` (`query` gains `--json`
      and defaults to Abbey's own store); `stats`/`checkpoint` answered in-process.
      Verified live against a locally built `abi-cli`: `query`, `db verify`, `compute info`,
      exit-code propagation, and a cross-check that `abi` reads the same 40 records the
      in-process backend wrote
- [x] Cross-process safety extends to the bridge: an `abbey wdbx` passthrough aimed at Abbey's
      own store takes the same lock, so Abbey's own CLI can't route around its guard. TUI
      redraw opens with a 250 ms timeout and reports `unavailable:` instead of "empty"
- [x] Cross-process safety: `fs4` advisory lock on `<store>/abbey.lock` held for the
      handle's life (Unix `flock`, Windows `LockFileEx`).
      Without it 20 concurrent `abbey` processes interleaved WAL appends and left the store
      **permanently unreadable** (CRC mismatch, every later open failed); with it 40/40
      concurrent writes land. SQLite passed the same test unaided — the lock is what makes
      the backends equivalent
- [x] Path convention: `abi` takes BASE paths (dir + base name), Abbey opens a directory —
      `<state>/wdbx/` is `<state>/wdbx/wdbx` to `abi`. The bridge translates so a bare
      directory can't silently read one level up and report an empty store
- [x] Doctor lines for backend path/status + whether the feature is linked; no SEA/learn
      duplication in Abbey
- [x] `check.sh` extended with `--features wdbx` clippy + test (the default run never
      compiles the gated code, so it could otherwise rot silently)

- [x] Doctor: persona prior, role bindings (Max→id, Gemma→id), memory backend
- [x] Hybrid visual+code loop: `abbey hybrid-loop` runs Gemma interpret → Max implement;

### 2026-10-22 — the rest of the review-thread triage

The remaining unresolved review threads on the merged PRs #45, #80, #89, #90,
#92, #94, #96, #98, #99, and #103 are twenty-five threads over twenty-two
distinct issues. Every one of them now carries a disposition reply on GitHub;
the ones that are still real are listed here so the disposition is durable in
the repository:

- [ ] **The wire schemas do not cover every vocabulary they now carry** (#94
      "Version every wire surface for the new statuses", #98 "Version every
      protocol that gains lifecycle statuses", #80 "Version the new protocol-v3
      operation state"). The shared `ClaimStatus` reaches protocol v1 and
      protocol v3, and the model inventory gained a `not_downloaded` value, but
      `APP_SCHEMA_V1` and `APP_SCHEMA_V3` were not bumped: an older client
      negotiates successfully and then fails to _decode_ the response. The fix
      is the two schema bumps plus the matching claim-row updates (the rows
      state that protocol v1 and v2 stay unchanged, and one row's next action
      says to preserve the exact protocol-v1 read-only wire schema).
- [ ] **The ledger cannot name which evidence channel lapsed or failed** (#94
      "Let expired claims request the evidence channel that lapsed", #98
      "Preserve valid local evidence when external proof fails").
      `local_live` and `external_required` are independent states with no
      per-channel failure marker, so a claim whose _external_ proof failed
      cannot be `Failed` while keeping its verified local evidence.
- [ ] **The TUI provider switch does not recompute the model** (#99 "Recompute
      the model when cycling away from Ollama"). `select_provider` resets the
      model for the `fm` transitions only, so cycling Ollama → Grok/Cursor
      leaves the Ollama tag in `cfg.model` and it reaches the Cursor grammar.
- [ ] **The captured-prompt clamp and the supervisor's argument budget
      disagree** (#99 "Keep captured prompt limits aligned with the host
      clamp"). The public host clamp is 96 KiB on Unix; the supervisor's
      `ProcessSpec` validator refuses an argument over 32 KiB and a total over
      64 KiB, so a 32–96 KiB prompt is accepted by the clamp and then refused
      by the validator. Which bound moves is an owner decision.
- [ ] **The Ollama readiness probe is unavailable off Unix** (#99 "Probe Ollama
      readiness without the Unix-only supervisor"). The supervisor is an
      `Unsupported` stub on Windows, so the probe always reports "not ready".
      The portable capture path is now bounded and tested on every host
      (`src/agent/bounded_capture.rs`), so the probe can use it off Unix — but
      no Windows host runs this gate, so the wiring needs a Windows
      acceptance.
- [ ] **The readiness probe runs for local-only verbs** (#99 "Avoid probing
      Ollama while dispatching local-only verbs") and **it ignores the
      requested tag** (#99 "Consider the requested tag when choosing the Ollama
      backend"). Both are fixed by deferring the probe until the effective
      model is known, which changes when the backend is resolved rather than
      what it resolves.
- [ ] **The `portable-primary-host-surfaces` claim overstates macOS voice
      coverage** (#103 "Do not claim a macOS portable voice fallback").
      `voice::speak` and `voice::listen` select the portable adapters only
      when `!is_macos()`, so on macOS they are never a fallback and the macOS
      branches fail directly.
- [ ] **The corpus schemas' identifier and digest patterns are unanchored**
      (#89 "Anchor bounded identifier patterns", #96 "Anchor the v2 identifier
      and digest patterns"). A JSON Schema `pattern` is a substring match, so
      `junksha256:<64 hex>suffix` satisfies the digest pattern. The schemas
      are digest-covered corpus bytes vendored from the sibling ABI
      repository, so anchoring them is an upstream change plus a re-vendored,
      re-qualified corpus and a new aggregate digest.
- [ ] **The corpus README documents a verification command that does not
      exist** (#89 "Provide the documented corpus verification command"). The
      README is a digest-covered corpus artifact, so the correction belongs
      upstream with the corpus.
- [ ] **The corpus golden vectors are never computed** (#89 "Exercise golden
      vectors before returning Valid"). Neither the JCS canonical bytes nor
      the independent corpus digest is compared against the fixture's
      `expected_hex` / `expected_digest`, so a document the unconstrained root
      schema accepts falls through to `Valid`.
- [ ] **The Program 3 engine advertises alternatives that produce empty
      plans** (#92 "Do not advertise empty permission alternatives"), **its
      rollback preview loses overwrite absence** (#92 "Preserve overwrite
      absence in rollback previews"), **its visibility evidence does not bind
      the bot's authority inputs** (#92 "Bind visibility evidence to bot
      authority inputs"), **it allocates a recording before bounding it**
      (#92 "Bound JSON before allocating the recording"), and **it accepts
      cyclic channel parents** (#92 "Reject cyclic channel parent
      relationships"). Each is a change to the closed synthetic engine, whose
      per-object digests and evidence are what the
      `program-3-guild-intelligence-synthetic` row claims.
- [ ] **The accelerator dylib is shared between the editions** (#45 "Keep the
      accelerator dylib edition-scoped"). Both editions install into the same
      default directory and load one fixed `@loader_path/libabi_metal_dot.dylib`
      path, so installing one edition replaces the file the other loads. The
      file name is fixed by the link-time install name, so the fix is an
      isolated install directory per edition — a packaging decision.
- [ ] **The v3 model request bounds and validation are narrower than the
      contract states** (#90 "Bound model payloads by serialized frame size",
      #90 "Allow standard multiline prompt whitespace", #90 "Preserve budget
      exhaustion error codes"). The 32 KiB bound is checked against the
      unserialized prompt, the prompt rejects every control character (so a
      multiline instruction cannot be submitted at all), and every inference
      failure is mapped to one generic error, so a budget-exhausted run is
      indistinguishable from any other. The last one is also coupled to the
      pinned ABI revision, whose `RunContext::finish` reports
      `StopReason::Completed` without consulting the elapsed duration.
- [ ] **The model artifact storage root is not edition-scoped** (#80 "Keep the
      model artifact storage root edition-scoped"). The root is resolved by the
      sibling ABI crate's `StorageRoot` (keyed on `ABI_MODELS_DIR`), so the
      safe and personal editions share one model store; the fix is a
      cross-repo, edition-qualified variable.
